facts.text: The restless flycatcher is nicknamed the razor grinder or scissors grinder thanks to its distinctive call.
facts.quote: it is also known as the razor grinder or scissors grinder because of its distinctive call.

facts.text: It is about 20 cm long, with a glossy dark blue crest, a grey-blue back and white underparts.
facts.quote: It is about 20 cm (8 in) long, with a glossy dark blue crest, a grey-blue back and white underparts.

facts.text: It resembles the willie wagtail but lacks a black throat and white eyebrow, and has a slenderer body shape.
facts.quote: It is similar to the willie wagtail, though the lack of a black throat, crest on head, white eyebrow and slenderer body shape are distinguishing features.

facts.text: It builds a cup-shaped nest from shredded bark and grasses, bound together with spider-webbing.
facts.quote: The restless flycatcher builds a cup-shaped nest from shredded bark and grasses, matted and bound with spider-webbing.

facts.text: Nests are often decorated with lichen, strips of bark or spiders' egg sacs.
facts.quote: It is often decorated with lichen, strips of bark or spiders' egg sacs.

facts.text: It lays three glossy light-grey to white eggs with brown or dark spots at the larger end.
facts.quote: They will lay three, light-grey to white glossy eggs with brown or dark spots at the larger end.

facts.text: It often hovers with its head and tail pointed downwards as it picks insects off leaves.
facts.quote: It often hovers with its head and tail pointed downwards as it picks insects off from leaves, and it rarely goes to the ground, preferring to hunt insects from mid-canopy.

facts.text: Its diet includes insects plus other invertebrates such as spiders and centipedes.
facts.quote: The restless flycatcher feeds on insects, as well as other invertebrates such as spiders and centipedes and will feed alone or in pairs.

facts.text: In winter, many southern populations move further north.
facts.quote: During winter many south and south-eastern populations move further north.

facts.text: The Yuwaalaraay people of northern New South Wales call this bird garaayaa.
facts.quote: The Yuwaalaraay people of northern New South Wales use the name garaayaa to refer to this species.
